covered_by.title: Erdős 897: fix growth hypothesis, log-growth conclusion and additive …
covered_by.note: The PR replaces the joint `(p, k)` product-filter limsup in `erdos_897.parts.i`, `parts.ii`, `variants.parts.i` and `variants.parts.ii` with a single definition `LimsupPrimePowEqTop`, a limsup over prime powers `q → ∞` with `IsPrimePow q`, which is our first two findings. It changes `variants.log_growth`'s conclusion from `f n ≤ c * Real.log n + O n` to the equality `f n = c * Real.log n + O n` with `O =O[atTop] 1`, our third finding. It replaces the `(∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p)` disjunct, which quantifies over `k = 0`, by `f.IsStronglyAdditive` (new in ForMathlib, requiring `k ≥ 1`) or `f.IsCompletelyAdditive` in both variants, our last two findings; the PR body credits this project's review.

covered_by.title: fix(OEIS/167918): ask whether the ratio is bounded, state existence
covered_by.note: The PR restates `conjecture2` as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n > 0 → S (a n) / S n ≤ C`, so boundedness is now an open yes/no question rather than an asserted affirmative, which is exactly our finding; its description cites OEIS comment (5a) as asking, not conjecturing, boundedness. It also drops the global totality hypothesis `∀ n > 0, a n ≠ 0` and adds a separate `conjecture_infinite : ∀ n > 0, ∃ k > n, S n ∣ S k` for OEIS comment (1). It landed on main at 4a7594e9 on 2026-09-22, after the reviewed commit 78231281 (2026-09-21), and credits this project's AI review.

covered_by.title: Paper/Homogenous: `countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable`: ω-monolithic, not monolithic
covered_by.note: This project's own issue from the c90271f0 review, still open, reports exactly the present finding: `countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable` assumes only `CountablyMonolithicSpace X` (metrizable closures of countable subsets), whereas Problem 17 of [Ar2013] concerns monolithic compact spaces, where the closure of every subset of infinite cardinality κ has weight at most κ.

covered_by.title: fix(Paper/Homogenous): Problem 17 concerns monolithic, not ω-monolithic, spaces
covered_by.note: The open PR adds `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Topology/CardinalInvariants.lean` (networks, `density`, `networkWeight`), defines `MonolithicSpace X` as `networkWeight Y ≤ density Y` for every subspace, and restates Problem 17 under `MonolithicSpace X`, renaming the declaration to `monolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable` and correcting its docstring. That is precisely our finding: the ω-monolithic hypothesis `CountablyMonolithicSpace X` is replaced by genuine monolithicity, while `Nonempty X`, compactness, Hausdorffness and the first-countable-point conclusion are kept. It states `Fixes #5699`.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/Falconer): falconer_conjecture is false at d = 1
covered_by.note: The open pull request adds the hypothesis `(h2d : 2 ≤ d)` to `falconer_conjecture`, which currently quantifies over every `d : ℕ`, and rewrites the module and declaration docstrings to state that restriction. Its justification is the same kind of counterexample as our finding: a base-7 Cantor set on digits {0,1,2} in ℝ with `dim_H E = log 3 / log 7 > 1/2` whose difference set, hence distance set, is null. `falconer_conjecture_two` is left untouched, exactly as our suggested fix says. That is the file's only misformalization.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/ModularityConjecture): use period 1 in the q-expansion
covered_by.note: The PR changes the body of `ModularityConjecture.modularFormAn` from `(qExpansion N f).coeff n` to `(qExpansion 1 f).coeff n` and adds a docstring saying that the first argument of `qExpansion` is the period at infinity, which is 1 for Γ₀(N), not the level. That is exactly our finding, and the PR body gives the same reasoning (for N > 1 the coefficient a₁ vanishes, so `IsNormalisedEigenform` is unsatisfiable and `modularityConjecture E` is false for every E), together with a compiled Lean refutation of the current statement. The PR is open and unmerged; the file is otherwise unchanged since the reviewed commit.

covered_by.title: Wikipedia/RudinsConjecture: counterexample to rudins_conjecture_unique at N = 6
covered_by.note: The open issue reports that `rudins_conjecture_unique`'s hypothesis `hN : 6 ≤ N` makes the statement false, exhibiting `(N, q, a) = (6, 120, 49)` attaining `Qmax 6 = 4` with `q ≠ 24`; a comment adds a second witness `(6, 168, 121)`, tabulates the argmax sets for `6 ≤ N ≤ 30` and identifies the source's restriction to `N = GP_k + 1 ≥ 8` as the root cause. That is our finding, including the observation that merely raising the bound to 8 is insufficient.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/RudinsConjecture): state uniqueness at N = GP_k + 1 ≥ 8
covered_by.note: The open PR replaces `hN : 6 ≤ N` in `rudins_conjecture_unique` by `hN : 8 ≤ N` together with `hN' : ∃ k : ℤ, (N : ℤ) = k * (3 * k - 1) / 2 + 1`, i.e. the generalized-pentagonal index restriction of González-Jiménez and Xarles, and rewrites the docstring to attribute the statement to the super-strong form and to record the `N = 6` failure. It includes a compiled Lean refutation of the statement as written. This is our finding and its suggested fix; it says `fixes #4568`.
